issues.body: `reconcile_dispatch_head` extracts and validates only `object.sha`; it still never checks `object.type`. Consequently payloads such as `{"object":{"sha":"<40 lowercase hex>","type":"tag"}}`, or the same object with `type` absent, are accepted as an authoritative commit head. This is materially identical to the round-4 major finding. The new fixtures place `type: "commit"` in successful fake responses, but the reducer ignores that value and the malformed-payload table has no valid-SHA tag, missing-type, or invalid-type case, so the trust check remains absent and untested through both outcome paths.
issues.fix_hint: Require `node.get("type") == "commit"` together with the exact 40-lowercase-hex SHA validation. Add negative reducer tests for a valid SHA with `type: "tag"`, missing `type`, and another invalid type, asserting `WorkerPrError`; also drive non-commit payloads through both review and fix outcome paths and assert `malformed-head` with no mutation.
issues.title: Branch-ref reducer still accepts non-commit Git objects

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-4 trust failure remains unchanged. `reconcile_dispatch_head` still treats any object carrying a syntactically valid SHA as a commit without validating `object.type`. The positive fixtures include `type: "commit"`, but the reducer ignores it and no negative type cases exercise the required fail-closed behavior.
